text:
Casey: quick flag: found a bunch of "projectless" API keys that are being billed to the org's default project in the dashboard. it's skewing a few customers' cost reports.
Maya: yup I noticed anomalies in the nightly usage rollup. router uses org.default_project as a last-resort for routing which makes sense for enforcement but not for billing attribution.
Dev: we never recorded provenance separately. router just emits `project` tag. suggestion: emit `project_provenance` + `project_value`. provenance can be asserted|token|fallback.
Priya: security note 3: we need to ensure any "asserted" value is cryptographically provable. otherwise anyone can hit the gateway with x-asserted-project.
Sam: agreed. plan: auth-service will produce a short-lived signed assertion header `x-project-assertion` (compact JWT) when it sees an explicit project in the token exchange path. gateway verifies and uses it for attribution only. routing enforcement still uses the computed effective project.
SecBot: checklist: (1) JWT signed by auth-service ksk, (2) TTL <= 5s, (3) nonce or jti to prevent replay, (4) gateway must verify `iss` and signature, (5) audits logged to audit-log stream.
Maya: UI idea: in the usage table add an "Attribution" pill: green=ASSERTED, amber=TOKEN, grey=FALLBACK. hovering shows source and confidence score (2/1/0). also allow filtering by attribution source.
Dev: pseudo router code:
```
// header is compact signed JWT or absent
if (verifyJwtHeader('x-project-assertion')) {
  attribution = 'asserted'
  project = jwt.claims.project
  confidence = 2
} else if (token.claims.project) {
  attribution = 'token'
  project = token.claims.project
  confidence = 1
} else {
  attribution = 'fallback'
  project = org.default_project
  confidence = 0
}
emit('request.attribution', 'project='+project+',prov='+attribution+',conf='+confidence+',org='+org.id)
```
Priya: cryptography perf: prefer mTLS between auth-service and gateway for assertion transport, or sign with HMAC key validated by gateway (faster than asymmetric per-request). but still need replay protection. jti works.
Sam: telemetry: emit both `billing_project` and `enforcement_project` tags for downstream pipelines. add event `attribution_switched` when attribution changes vs historical. backfill plan: recompute last 14 days for affected orgs to keep billing UI consistent during canary.
Casey: rollout: gate under feature flag `attrib_signed_assertions_v1`. rollout steps: staging -> canary 5% orgs -> monitor attribution deltas and billing pipeline differences -> expand. need to coordinate with finance so invoices don't differ unexpectedly.
Maya: for console, default filter should hide FALLBACK unless user opts in. add small explainer tooltip about why some rows are FALLBACK.
Dev: quick perf note: verification adds ~1ms if using HMAC, ~3-4ms for RSA verify. batch issuance is cheap since auth-service issues JWTs only on token exchange, not every request. also we can cache verified assertions for a few seconds keyed by jti to avoid crypto on repeated calls.
Priya: security sign-off conditioned on: signed assertions + audit log + replay protection + no PII in claims (only project id). put this checklist in PR template.
Sam: I'll open the RFC with telemetry schema, dashboard mocks, and backfill job outline.
Casey: deploy-bot, flip the flag in staging when ready and run smoke against projectless keys.
deploy-bot: feature flag attrib_signed_assertions_v1 enabled in staging :white_check_mark: smoke tests scheduled.
Casey: action items:
- Sam: RFC + backfill + telemetry dashboards
- Dev: gateway + router changes + assertion verification + cache
- Priya: signature spec + security checklist for PR
- Maya: console UX mock + default filter behavior
- Casey: sync with finance on billing backfill approach
Casey: target canary next Wednesday, full rollout contingent on two weeks of clean telemetry. thanks everyone.
